rows.note: Launch plan storage, billed per GB-month with no included allowance. Lineup checked 2026-08-30: Neon publishes Free, Launch and Scale; Launch and Scale are both 'Pay for what you use' with 'no monthly minimum' and the same $0.35/GB-month storage rate, so no cheaper plan can win these workloads.
Launch plan public network transfer (egress): 500 GB per project included, then $0.10/GB.
Pro plan base subscription: 'From $25/month' for the first project (includes $10/mo compute credit covering one Micro instance).
Pro plan disk size: 8 GB included per project, then $0.125 per GB.
Pro plan egress: 250 GB included, then $0.09 per GB.
PlanetScale Postgres HA (3-node: 1 primary + 2 replicas) cluster fee for the PS-80 arm64 SKU (1 vCPU, 8 GiB memory) in AWS us-east-1, from the official pricing table.

Postgres HA network-attached storage: first 10 GB free, then billed per GB beyond that; rate derived exactly from the live pricing calculator's computed total (delta of $375 for +1000 GB, i.e. $0.375/GB, independent of cluster SKU size).
Postgres HA egress bandwidth: '100 GB of egress bandwidth is included. Additional usage: $0.06/GB.'

PlanetScale Postgres EBS single node (non-HA), the cheapest paid Postgres cluster: 'PS-5 / 1/16 vCPU / 512 MB memory / 10 GB storage / $5 / Includes 1 node' in the AWS us-east-1 calculator, matching the published SKU table ('Postgres EBS non-HA (single node)': PS-5 x86-64 and PS-5 arm64 both $5). Calculator's estimated monthly total at the default 10 GB storage and 10 GB egress is $5.

Postgres EBS network-attached storage on a single node: 'the first 10 GB is free, with per-GB pricing beyond that'. Rate derived exactly from the live calculator's estimated monthly total, holding egress at its 10 GB included level: 1010 GB storage gives $130 against a $5 base, i.e. $125 for 1000 GB beyond the included 10 GB = $0.125/GB. One third of the $0.375/GB HA rate, which provisions the volume on all three nodes.

Single-node PS-5 egress bandwidth: '10 GB of egress bandwidth is included. Additional usage: $0.06 / GB.' The included allowance is SKU-specific and lower than the HA cluster's 100 GB. Confirmed against the calculator total: 1010 GB egress gives $65 against a $5 base, i.e. $60 for 1000 GB = $0.06/GB.
Entry PostgreSQL plan at $15.15/month; the base tier includes a 10 GiB to 30 GiB storage range. attributes.storage_gib records the floor of that range, 10 GiB, not the full range.
Storage expansion beyond the plan's included 10 GiB, quoted as $0.215/GiB/mo and sold in 10 GiB increments.
Essential 1 plan at $9/month including 10 GB of storage; Essential tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Essential 0 plan at $5/month including 1 GB of storage; Essential tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Essential 2 plan at $20/month including 32 GB of storage; Essential tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Standard 0 plan at $50/month including 64 GB of storage and 4 GB of memory; Standard tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Standard 2 plan at $200/month including 256 GB of storage and 8 GB of memory; Standard tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Standard 3 plan at $400/month including 512 GB of storage and 15 GB of memory; Standard tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Premium 2 plan at $350/month including 256 GB of storage and 8 GB of memory; Premium tiers bundle storage with no separate per-GB charge.
Developer plan base fee, the cheapest paid tier: 'Developer / $4.99/month'.
Developer plan storage: 'Storage ... 9GB / + $0.75 / GB'. Page states 'GB' with no GiB/binary clarification.

Pay as You Go storage: 'For each database, the first 1GB is free. Beyond that, storage is charged at $0.25 per GB of total storage.' No fixed monthly fee exists for this plan, so no plan_base_month row is recorded.
Pay as You Go bandwidth: 'For pay-as-you-go, monthly bandwidth is free up to 200GB. Beyond that, we charge $0.03 per additional GB.'

M10 Dedicated cluster tier card: '$0.08/hour ... Starts at $56.94/month', confirmed with Storage 10 GB / RAM 2 GB / vCPUs 2 bundled at this tier (cross-checked against the Dedicated Cluster storage-range modal showing M10: 10-128 GB). $56.94/month is a derived monthly floor from the hourly rate, not a native flat monthly SKU, hence medium confidence. Storage-overage and egress rates are NOT recorded: MongoDB's own docs give no flat per-GB figure for either (storage overage docs say only 'charges for the full amount' with no rate; data-transfer docs give 'Out to Internet: $0.09 to $0.16' per GB as a range, confirmed live on https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/billing/data-transfer-costs/).

Performance tier card: 'Storage priced at $0.177 / GB-month', metered from actual usage with no stated included allowance. Reached via a permanent redirect from https://www.timescale.com/pricing (Timescale has rebranded to Tiger Data / Tiger Cloud). plan_base_month is NOT recorded: the card's 'Compute starts at $30/month' is an hourly-metered floor for the smallest instance size, not a fixed recurring fee independent of usage, so entering it as plan_base_month would misrepresent it. egress_gib is NOT recorded: confirmed live via in-page text search that neither 'egress' nor 'transfer' appears anywhere on the page.

Hobby-0 instance tier on AWS, the cheapest paid tier in the itemized table: 'Cores 2 | Memory .5GB | Price $9'. The page's own top banner separately advertises 'plans starting at $10/mo' -- a $1 discrepancy with this itemized table figure; $9 is recorded because it comes from the line-item table, not the marketing banner.

'Storage costs are $0.10 per GB. For example, 100 GB would be $10 per month.' No included allowance is stated on this page for any instance tier, so included_allowance is recorded as 0; medium confidence because a minimum provisioned volume size is common for block-storage-backed Postgres and was not explicitly ruled out or confirmed via the pricing calculator.

Verbatim: 'Prices include infrastructure, backups, and data transfer.' Data transfer (egress) is bundled into every instance tier's price at no separate per-GB charge -- first-party evidence of a known zero, confirmed live on the page.

Startup-4 sub-tier -- the specific SKU behind the headline 'STARTUP starting from $75/month' -- confirmed via the 'View 7 plans' breakdown: 'Startup-4 | 1 | 2 | 4GB | 80 - 400 GB | $0.10 | $75'. attributes.storage_gib records the floor of the 80-400 GB range, matching this dataset's convention for a range-bundled plan (see DigitalOcean's row). Aiven's FAQ recommends Startup as the minimum plan for production workloads.

Verbatim: 'All networking cost included.' Confirmed via the plan comparison table that this feature is checked (available) for every paid PostgreSQL plan including Startup. First-party evidence of a known zero -- Aiven's pricing is explicitly 'all-inclusive', with no per-GB networking charge on any tier.

Startup-8 sub-tier, confirmed via the 'View 7 plans' breakdown: 'Startup-8 | 1 | 4 | 8GB | 175 - 875 GB | $0.20 | $145'. Recorded specifically because it is the cheapest Aiven PostgreSQL tier whose floor storage allotment meets or exceeds 100 GiB -- Startup-4's 80 GB floor falls short, so recording only Startup-4 would have produced a coverage gap against the plan-with-100gib-storage shape workload (the exact failure mode this dataset has previously published as a $150 error).
Verbatim: 'All networking cost included.' Same first-party bundled-zero evidence as the startup-4 row, recorded again under this plan name so the fact is visible against the startup-8 group too.

Starter plan base fee: 'Starter / $10/month'. This fee is a combined platform charge covering both Prisma Postgres and the separate Prisma Compute app-hosting product's included allowances; it is not possible to isolate a database-only portion, but this matches how Prisma itself bills (one bill, no split).
Starter plan Prisma Postgres storage: '10 GB storage, then $2.00 per GB' (comparison table: 'Storage included | 10 GB', 'Storage overage | $2.00 per GB').

Verbatim: 'Unlimited Prisma Postgres data transfer' listed under 'Every plan includes'; comparison table also shows 'Data transfer | Unlimited' across all plans. This is the database's own data transfer and is unlimited/free; it is distinct from the separate Prisma Compute product's metered 'Outbound bandwidth' ($0.025/GB), which is a different product line and not recorded here as database egress.

Business plan: '$129/month', comparison table 'Storage included | 100GB'. The page does not state whether GB is decimal or binary; recorded as decimal (100 x 10^9 bytes = 93.13 GiB), the conservative reading. Under a binary reading this plan would provide exactly 100 GiB.
Scaler plan base fee, quoted as '$24.92/month' with '24GB' storage included.
Scaler storage overage, quoted as '$0.50 / GB' beyond the 24GB included in the plan.
